title: Exponential & Logarithmic Expressions
summary: Exponential expressions $a^x$ grow or decay by a constant factor; logarithms invert them: $\log_a x=y$ means $a^y=x$. The log laws turn products, quotients, and powers into sums, differences, and multiples, and let you solve exponential equations.

exponential expression.plain: A constant raised to a variable power.

product law.plain: Log of a product is a sum of logs.

quotient law.plain: Log of a quotient is a difference.

power law.plain: Log of a power pulls the exponent out.

change of base.plain: Rewrite a log in another base.

concept_sections.heading: Exponential expressions
concept_sections.explanation: $a^x$ multiplies by $a$ each time $x$ increases by 1 — growth if $a>1$, decay if $0<a<1$. The base sets the rate; the exponent sets how many steps.
math_steps: Evaluate by repeated multiplication or exponent laws.

concept_sections.heading: Logarithms as inverses
concept_sections.explanation: $\log_a x=y$ asks 'what power of $a$ gives $x$?' It undoes the exponential: $a^{\log_a x}=x$ and $\log_a(a^x)=x$.
math_steps: Use inverses to cancel matching bases.

concept_sections.heading: The log laws
concept_sections.explanation: Products become sums, quotients become differences, and powers become coefficients: $\log(MN)=\log M+\log N$, $\log\tfrac{M}{N}=\log M-\log N$, $\log M^p=p\log M$.

concept_sections.heading: Change of base
concept_sections.explanation: To evaluate $\log_a x$ on a calculator, use $\log_a x=\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln a}$ (or with $\log_{10}$). It also rewrites logs into a common base.

concept_sections.heading: Solving exponential equations
concept_sections.explanation: Take a logarithm of both sides to bring the variable exponent down, then solve the resulting linear equation.
math_steps: Use the power law to free the exponent, then solve.

real_world_examples.title: Compound interest
real_world_examples.scenario: Money grows by a fixed percent each year.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Balance is exponential $P(1+r)^t$; logs solve for the time to reach a goal.

real_world_examples.title: Carbon dating
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The remaining fraction is exponential; a logarithm recovers the elapsed time.
